prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create one premium textbook editorial mechanism illustration for an article about an AI engineering academy teaching forward-deployed engineers to translate customer business processes into reliable AI software. Explain learning by doing software delivery, not physical fieldwork. The reader must immediately understand that these are AI software engineering skills practiced in real customer workflows. This is an illustrative learning model, not a claim about a vendor's exact curriculum.

Canvas: exactly 1200 by 630 pixels, landscape 40:21, opaque pure white background. Fill the canvas with a coherent, richly detailed, polished technical illustration; crisp at article viewing size, generous internal spacing, no empty expanses, no clutter or overlapping labels. Sophisticated clean editorial vector-like 3D/isometric software interface panels with restrained blue, teal, violet, amber accents, fine navy connector lines, soft subtle shadows. No decorative filler. No photos, people, faces, humanoids, mascots, logos, brand names, factories, ships, ports, mountains, outdoor landscapes, physical field exercises, construction, or industrial hardware.

Composition: five substantial interconnected software workstations across the top two-thirds, each comprising several layered but clearly separated miniature application views. Short accurate headings above them, exactly: "Customer workflow", "AI prototype", "Evaluation", "Deployment", "Feedback". They form an explicit causal left-to-right progression, with a clear feedback return loop below to the prototype. The illustrations must be concrete and software-specific:
1 Customer workflow: a support-request inbox, branching business process, structured knowledge documents, data schema with linked fields, and an outlined scope boundary. Connect a highlighted customer request and permitted knowledge to prototype.
2 AI prototype: split software editor and application preview; separate prompt/instructions card, retrieved context cards, tool connector nodes, and a visible sample response card. Fine connector lines show how prompt + context + tool result compose the response.
3 Evaluation: multiple test-case cards feeding a comparison matrix; distinct expected-versus-observed response columns; green pass checks and amber failure markers; a tiny inspected error trace; an amber revision arrow returns a failed case to prototype. This is the largest visual anchor. Use schematic marks only, never tiny pseudo-writing.
4 Deployment: staged software release cards linked in order, a compact access-permission matrix and shield lock, a monitored application dashboard, and an explicit approval/checkpoint symbol. Clearly a controlled SOFTWARE release, no warehouse or physical structure.
5 Feedback: anonymized usage-event tiles, quality observation cards, a short issue-priority queue, and versioned revision cards. A prominent curved return arrow routes evidence back to the prototype and its test cases.

Bottom third: an integrated skills-to-practice evidence map, not a giant title or sparse decorative strip. Five aligned clusters corresponding to the workstations above. Exact readable labels: "Problem framing", "Prompt + context", "Test + improve", "Release safely", "Learn from use". Under each label, depict a compact stack of worked exercise artifacts, a three-row competency grid with filled cells, and an evidence check marker. Connect each skills cluster vertically to its software workstation; show progression from practice artifacts to demonstrated capability. Add one small centered bottom label, exactly "Practice builds demonstrated capability".

At least twenty distinct meaningful visible technical components overall. Do not rely on repeated boxes or generic server stacks. Make every component explain a relationship: business need to scope, context to response, test case to evidence, gate to release, observation to revision. No numeric outcomes, fabricated curriculum names, long prose, title banner, or unapproved extra readable text. Use only the ten main labels plus the small bottom label specified. Keep all labels large, grammatically exact, legible, inside safe margins. The final illustration should feel like a detailed professional textbook figure about learning to engineer useful, tested, governed AI applications.
targeted_edit_prompt: Edit this AI-software engineering learning illustration. Preserve the full composition, five software-workflow stages, dense technical detail, pure white background, all ten main labels, the bottom caption and the software-learning meaning. Make only these strict corrections: remove EVERY human/avatar/person/silhouette/bust icon, including the two evaluation column header person icons, all access-matrix person icons in Deployment, and all three feedback user-circle icons. Replace the evaluation header icons with a blue document and green checklist respectively. Replace access-matrix row/column people with small document, key, shield, and application-grid glyphs. Replace feedback circles with small telemetry-event and document glyphs. Inspect the entire image: absolutely no head-and-shoulders icons, no stick figures, no people or humanoids anywhere. Also remove the tiny "v3", "v2", "v1" lettering from the revision timeline, retaining its dots and connecting line. Keep technical labels exactly as they are, crisp and readable. No brand logos, photos, landscapes or factory scenes. Final delivery is an opaque PNG, exactly 1200 pixels wide by 630 pixels high, full artwork fitted with safe margins and no cropping. This is the final professional textbook illustration of learning to build, evaluate, deploy and improve AI software.

creation_review.reason: Human silhouette icons appeared despite the no-people requirement.
creation_review.targeted_edit: Replaced silhouettes with document, key, shield and telemetry glyphs; removed unapproved version text.
